questions.question: The sign convention for focal length of a concave lens _________.
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**is negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is a **diverging lens** that possesses at least one surface that curves inwards. It causes parallel beams of light to spread out or diverge after passing through it.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **optical center** of the lens is considered the **origin (0,0)**, and all distances are measured from this point.
 
• Distances measured in the **direction of incident light** are taken as **positive**, while those measured **opposite to the direction of incident light** are taken as **negative**.
 
• The **principal focus** of a **concave lens** is the point from which the rays of light, originally parallel to the axis, appear to diverge after passing through the lens. This point lies on the **same side** as the incident light (usually the **left side**).
 
• Because the distance from the **optical center** to the **principal focus** is measured against the direction of the incident light, the **focal length** of a **concave lens** is always **negative**. ***Hence, the statement that the sign convention is negative is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention for Convex Lens**:
 
 
• A **convex lens** is a **converging lens**. Its **principal focus** is located on the **opposite side** of the incident light (right side).
 
• Therefore, the **focal length** of a **convex lens** is always considered **positive** under the standard sign convention.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification**:
 
 
• The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the **lens formula**: **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• The **magnification (m)** produced by a lens is the ratio of image height to object height, which also equals **v/u**. For a **concave lens**, the magnification is always **positive** and **less than one**.
 
 
 
• **Power of a Lens**:
 
 
• The **power** of a lens is defined as the **reciprocal of its focal length** in meters (**P = 1/f**).
 
• The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. Since the focal length of a **concave lens** is **negative**, its **optical power** is also **negative**.
 
• For example, a person with **Myopia** (near-sightedness) is prescribed **concave lenses** with **negative power** (e.g., -2.5 D).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Image Formation by Concave Lens**:
 
 
• A **concave lens** always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished image**, regardless of where the object is placed in front of it.
 
• The **image distance (v)** for a **concave lens** is always **negative** because the image is formed on the same side as the object.
 
 
 
• **Object Distance (u)**:
 
 
• By convention, the **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens. Consequently, the **object distance (u)** is **always negative** in calculations for both convex and concave lenses.

questions.question: Four resistors of 5 Omega , 15 Omega , 20 Omega and 40 Omega are connected in series. The equivalent resistance is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**80 Ω**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In an electrical circuit, when resistors are connected in **series**, they are arranged in a single continuous path, allowing the same **electric current** to flow through each component sequentially.
 
• The **equivalent resistance (Req)** of a series combination is the **algebraic sum** of the individual resistances. The mathematical formula used is **Req = R1 + R2 + R3 + ... + Rn**.
 
• According to the question, the four given resistors are **5 Ω**, **15 Ω**, **20 Ω**, and **40 Ω**.
 
• By applying the series formula: **Req = 5 Ω + 15 Ω + 20 Ω + 40 Ω**.
 
• Calculating the sum: **5 + 15 = 20 Ω**; then **20 + 20 = 40 Ω**; and finally **40 + 40 = 80 Ω**. ***Hence, the equivalent resistance is 80 Ω.***
 
• A fundamental characteristic of this arrangement is that the **total resistance** is always **greater** than the largest individual resistor in the circuit (in this case, 80 Ω is greater than 40 Ω).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law:** This law states that the current passing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points. It is expressed as **V = I × R**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance.
 
• **Parallel Combination:** If these resistors were connected in **parallel**, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance would be the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances (**1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3 + 1/R4**). In parallel, the equivalent resistance is always **smaller** than the smallest individual resistor.
 
• **Voltage Division:** In a **series circuit**, the total voltage provided by the source is shared among the resistors. Each resistor experiences a **voltage drop** proportional to its resistance value.
 
• **Unit of Resistance:** The **SI unit** of electrical resistance is the **Ohm**, symbolized by the Greek letter **Ω** (Omega), named after the German physicist **Georg Simon Ohm** who published his findings in **1827**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Current Consistency:** In a series circuit, the **current (I)** remains **constant** at every point. This means the same number of **electrons** flows through the 5 Ω resistor as through the 40 Ω resistor per unit of time.
 
• **Circuit Sensitivity:** One major disadvantage of a series connection is that if any one component **fails** or the path is broken (e.g., a fused bulb), the entire circuit becomes **open**, and the current stops flowing through all components.
 
• **Applications:** Series circuits are commonly used in **voltage dividers**, **fuses** for protection, and simple low-power electronic strings. However, they are rarely used in **household wiring** because of the failure risk and the shared voltage.
 
• **Total Power:** The total **power consumption** in a series circuit is the sum of the power dissipated by each resistor (**P_total = P1 + P2 + P3 + P4**).

questions.question: According to Newton’s Second Law of Motion, force is given by the relation F = ma . If a body’s velocity changes from u (initial velocity) to v (final velocity) in time t , which of the following expressions correctly gives the force acting on the body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F = m(v-u)/t**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the **Force (F)** acting on an object is mathematically defined as the product of its **mass (m)** and its **acceleration (a)**, expressed as **F = ma**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)** is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** with respect to **time (t)**. It is calculated by subtracting the **initial velocity (u)** from the **final velocity (v)** and dividing the result by the time interval. The formula is **a = (v - u) / t**.
 
• By substituting the formula for acceleration into the original equation of the **Second Law**, we derive **F = m * ((v - u) / t)**, which simplifies to **F = m(v - u) / t**. ***Hence, the expression in option 2 is correct.***
 
• This relation demonstrates that **Force** is proportional to the rate of change of **linear momentum**, where **mv** is the final momentum and **mu** is the initial momentum.
 
• Options 1, 3, and 4 are mathematically inconsistent with the definitions of **acceleration** and **Newton's Second Law**. ***Hence, statements 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**: Also known as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain at rest or continue to move at a constant **velocity** unless acted upon by an external **unbalanced force**.
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion**: This law states that for every **action**, there is always an **equal and opposite reaction**. These forces act on two different bodies.
 
• **Linear Momentum (p)**: It is a **vector quantity** defined as the product of **mass** and **velocity** (**p = mv**). The **SI unit** of momentum is **kg·m/s**.
 
• **SI Unit of Force**: The standard unit of **Force** is the **Newton (N)**. One **Newton** is the force required to provide an **acceleration** of **1 m/s²** to an object with a **mass** of **1 kg** (**1 N = 1 kg·m/s²**).
 
• **Impulse**: When a large **force** acts on a body for a very short **time**, the product of force and time is called **Impulse**, which is also equal to the total change in **momentum**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass vs. Weight**: **Mass** is a fundamental property of an object representing the amount of matter, while **Weight (W = mg)** is the **gravitational force** acting on that mass. **Mass** is **constant** everywhere, but **weight** changes based on the **acceleration due to gravity (g)**.
 
• **Vector Nature**: **Force**, **Acceleration**, and **Velocity** are all **vector quantities**, meaning they possess both **magnitude** and **direction**. In the formula **F = m(v-u)/t**, the direction of the **Force** is the same as the direction of the **acceleration**.
 
• **Retardation**: If the **final velocity (v)** is less than the **initial velocity (u)**, the **acceleration** becomes negative. This is known as **retardation** or **deceleration**, indicating that the **Force** is acting in the opposite direction of motion.
 
• **Applications**: The principle **F = m(v-u)/t** is used in designing **safety features** like **airbags** and **seatbelts** in cars. By increasing the **time (t)** taken to stop during a crash, the **Force (F)** exerted on the passengers is significantly reduced.

questions.question: An ultrasonic wave has a frequency of 33 kHz. What will be the wavelength of this wave, if its speed is 330 m/s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.01 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the wavelength of the ultrasonic wave, we use the fundamental wave equation: **Speed (v) = Frequency (f) x Wavelength (λ)**.
 
• The given **Frequency (f)** is **33 kHz**. Since **1 kHz = 1,000 Hz**, the frequency in the standard unit (SI) is **33,000 Hz**.
 
• The **Speed (v)** of the wave is provided as **330 m/s**.
 
• Rearranging the formula to solve for wavelength, we get: **Wavelength (λ) = Speed (v) / Frequency (f)**.
 
• Substituting the values into the equation: **λ = 330 / 33,000**.
 
• On calculation, **330 / 33,000 = 1 / 100 = 0.01 m**. ***Hence, the wavelength of the wave is 0.01 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ultrasonic Waves:** These are sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper audible limit of human hearing, which is typically **20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• **Nature of Sound:** Sound is a **longitudinal mechanical wave** that requires a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot travel through a **vacuum**.
 
• **Relationship between Parameters:** The **Speed** of a wave depends on the properties of the medium through which it travels, whereas the **Frequency** is determined by the source of the wave. The **Wavelength** is the distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions.
 
• **Applications of Ultrasound:** Because of their high frequency and short wavelength, ultrasonic waves are used in **Medical Imaging (Ultrasonography)**, **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) to measure ocean depth, and **Industrial cleaning** to remove dirt from spiral parts or electronic components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Classification of Sound based on Frequency:**
 
 
• **Infrasonic:** Frequencies below **20 Hz** (e.g., waves produced by **Rhinoceroses** or **Whales**).
 
• **Audible Range:** Frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz** for a normal human ear.
 
• **Ultrasonic:** Frequencies above **20,000 Hz** (e.g., waves used by **Bats** for navigation and prey detection).
 
 
 
• **Effect of Medium:** The **Speed of sound** is maximum in **solids** (like steel or aluminum), intermediate in **liquids** (like water), and minimum in **gases** (like air).
 
• **SI Units:** The SI unit of **Frequency** is **Hertz (Hz)**, **Wavelength** is **Meters (m)**, and **Speed** is **Meters per second (m/s)**. Always ensure units are converted to the SI system before calculation.

questions.question: Which method is commonly used for extracting moderately reactive metals such as iron from their ores?

options.text: Electrolysis performed on the molten form of metal oxide ores
Chemical reduction of the ore using carbon-based reducing agents
Dissolving and melting of the ore material in concentrated acids
Direct heating of the metallic ore strongly in the presence of air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical reduction of the ore using carbon-based reducing agents**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals located in the middle of the **reactivity series**, such as **Iron (Fe)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Lead (Pb)**, and **Tin (Sn)**, are considered **moderately reactive**.
 
• These metals are typically found in the Earth's crust as **sulphides**, **carbonates**, or **oxides**. Because it is easier to extract a metal from its oxide than from its sulphide or carbonate, the ores are first converted into metal oxides.
 
• The process of **chemical reduction** involves using a reducing agent, most commonly **carbon** (in the form of **coke**) or **carbon monoxide**, to remove oxygen from the metal oxide. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• In the industrial extraction of **Iron**, the ore (usually **Hematite, Fe2O3**) is reacted with **coke** in a **Blast Furnace**. The carbon reduces the iron oxide to molten iron.
 
• **Electrolysis** is reserved for highly reactive metals like **Sodium** and **Aluminum** because their affinity for oxygen is too strong to be broken by carbon. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Direct heating** in the presence of air (thermal decomposition) is only sufficient for metals of very low reactivity, such as **Mercury** or **Copper** found in their sulphide ores. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Dissolving ores in **concentrated acids** is generally part of **leaching** or **hydrometallurgical** processes but is not the primary common method for extracting bulk **iron**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series:** 
 
 
• This is a list of metals arranged in the order of their decreasing activities. Metals at the top (**Potassium, Sodium, Calcium**) are never found in nature as free elements and are extracted via **electrolytic reduction**.
 
• Metals at the bottom (**Gold, Silver, Platinum**) are the least reactive and often found in the **native state**.
 
 
 
• **Roasting and Calcination:**
 
 
• **Roasting**: The process of heating **sulphide ores** strongly in the presence of **excess air** to convert them into oxides. For example, **Zinc blende (ZnS)** is roasted to form **Zinc oxide (ZnO)**.
 
• **Calcination**: The process of heating **carbonate ores** strongly in **limited air** or the absence of air to convert them into oxides. For example, **Calamine (ZnCO3)** is calcined to produce **Zinc oxide (ZnO)**.
 
 
 
• **Reducing Agents:**
 
 
• While **Carbon (Coke)** is the most economical reducing agent, sometimes highly reactive metals like **Aluminum (Al)** are used as reducing agents in **displacement reactions**. 
 
• This is known as the **Thermite Process**, which is highly **exothermic** and used for specialized applications like **joining railway tracks** or cracked machine parts.
 
 
 
• **Extraction of Iron (Specifics):**
 
 
• The **Blast Furnace** operates at temperatures reaching up to **2000 K** near the base. 
 
• **Limestone (CaCO3)** is added as a **flux** to remove **silica (SiO2)** impurities, forming **slag (CaSiO3)**, which floats on top of the molten iron and is easily removed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Feasibility:** **Carbon** is used for moderately reactive metals because it is abundant and **inexpensive**. **Electrolysis**, while effective, requires massive amounts of **electricity**, making it too costly for metals that can be reduced chemically.
 
• **Oxidation-Reduction:** In these reactions, the metal ore is **reduced** (loses oxygen) while the reducing agent (carbon) is **oxidized** (gains oxygen to form CO or CO2).
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The use of carbon-based reduction in **metallurgy** is a major source of **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** emissions globally, leading to modern research into **Green Hydrogen** as an alternative reducing agent for the **Steel Industry**.
</ul

questions.question: Which pair of energy forms constitutes the total mechanical energy of an object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Potential energy and Kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is the sum of **Potential Energy** and **Kinetic Energy**. It is the energy associated with the **motion** and **position** of an object.
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is calculated using the formula **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents **mass** and **v** represents **velocity**. Any moving object, such as a rolling ball or a flying airplane, possesses this form of energy.
 
• **Potential Energy** is the stored energy of an object based on its **position**, **state**, or **configuration**. The most common form is **gravitational potential energy**, given by the formula **P.E. = mgh**, where **m** is **mass**, **g** is **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²**), and **h** is the **height** above a reference point.
 
• The **Total Mechanical Energy (E)** of a system is defined as **E = K + U**, where **K** is kinetic energy and **U** is potential energy. In an isolated system where only **conservative forces** (like gravity) are acting, the total mechanical energy remains **constant**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The other options involve forms of energy like **Heat**, **Chemical**, **Nuclear**, and **Electrical**, which are categorized as **non-mechanical** energy forms in this context because they relate to **microscopic** internal structures rather than the **macroscopic** motion or position of the object as a whole.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Potential energy and Kinetic energy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• This principle states that the **total mechanical energy** of an object remains **constant** if it is acted upon only by **conservative forces**. For example, as a **pendulum** swings, its **potential energy** is converted into **kinetic energy** and vice versa, but the **sum** remains the same (ignoring air resistance).
 
 
 
• **Forms of Potential Energy:**
 
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy:** Energy stored in objects like a compressed **spring** or a stretched **rubber band**. It depends on the **displacement** from the equilibrium position.
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:** Energy stored due to an object's **altitude**. A **raised hammer** or water stored in a **dam** are classic examples.
 
 
 
• **Non-Mechanical Energy Forms:**
 
 
• **Chemical Energy:** Energy stored in the **bonds** of chemical compounds (atoms and molecules). It is released during a **chemical reaction**, often in the form of **heat**. Examples include **batteries**, **biomass**, and **petroleum**.
 
• **Nuclear Energy:** Energy released during **nuclear fission** or **fusion**, originating from the **nucleus** of an atom.
 
• **Heat (Thermal) Energy:** The energy that comes from the **temperature** of the heated substance. It is the result of the **vibration** of atoms and molecules within substances.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Option 2:** **Heat** and **Chemical** energy are internal energies related to molecular motion and bonding, not macroscopic mechanical energy.
 
• **Option 3:** **Nuclear** and **Sound** energy are distinct forms; while sound is a mechanical wave, nuclear energy is subatomic.
 
• **Option 4:** **Electrical** and **Light** energy are **electromagnetic** in nature and do not constitute the standard "mechanical energy" definition of an object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit of Energy:** The **SI unit** for all forms of energy, including mechanical energy, is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**. This distinguishes it from **momentum** or **force**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the change in its **kinetic energy**. It is a fundamental concept in **classical mechanics**.
 
• **Numerical Fact:** **1 Joule** is defined as the work done by a **force** of **one Newton** acting through a **distance** of **one meter**.
 
• **Real-world Application:** In **hydroelectric power plants**, the **potential energy** of water stored at a **height** is converted into **kinetic energy** as it falls, which then turns **turbines** to generate **electricity**.
</ul

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed exactly at the **Principal Focus (F1)** of a **convex lens**, the light rays emerging from the object travel through the lens and emerge **parallel** to each other on the other side.
 
• Since **parallel rays** are mathematically considered to meet at **infinity**, the position of the image is said to be at **infinity**. *Hence, the statement in option 2 is correct.*
 
• The **nature of the image** formed in this scenario is **real and inverted**. This is because the rays are refracting through the lens and would eventually converge (at infinity) on the side opposite to the object.
 
• Regarding the **size of the image**, it is described as being **highly enlarged** or **infinitely large**. As the rays travel further away, the height of the intersection point relative to the principal axis increases drastically.
 
• This principle is the foundation for devices that require a **parallel beam of light**, such as **searchlights** or **theatrical spotlights**, where the light source is placed at the focus of a converging lens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):**
 
 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the **center** than at the **edges**. It converges incident light rays that are parallel to the principal axis to a specific point called the **focus**.
 
• The behavior of the image changes based on the **object distance (u)** relative to the **focal length (f)**.
 
 
 
• **Other Image Formations in Convex Lenses:**
 
 
• **Object between Focus (F) and Optical Center (O):** The image is formed on the **same side** as the object. It is **virtual, erect, and magnified**. *This corresponds to option 1.*
 
• **Object at 2F:** The image is formed at **2F** on the other side. It is **real, inverted, and exactly the same size** as the object. *This contradicts option 3 and 4.*
 
• **Object between F and 2F:** The image is formed **beyond 2F**. It is **real, inverted, and magnified**. *This is often confused with the focus position.*
 
• **Object Beyond 2F:** The image is formed **between F and 2F** on the opposite side. It is **real, inverted, and diminished**.
 
 
 
• **The Lens Formula:**
 
 
• The relationship between the focal length (**f**), object distance (**u**), and image distance (**v**) is given by the formula: **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• For an object at focus, **u = -f**. Applying the formula: 1/v - 1/(-f) = 1/f, which results in **1/v = 0**, meaning **v = infinity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object (**h'/h**), or **v/u**. When the image is at **infinity**, the **magnification is infinite**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **focal length** of a convex lens is always taken as **positive**, while for a concave lens, it is **negative**.
 
• **Real vs Virtual:** A **real image** can be caught on a **screen** and is formed by the actual intersection of light rays. A **virtual image** cannot be caught on a screen and is formed when rays appear to diverge from a point.
 
• **Power of a Lens:** It is the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (**P = 1/f**). The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**.
</ul

questions.question: A passenger in a moving bus falls forward when the bus suddenly stops. This is due to which of the following?

options.text: Inertia of motion of the passenger

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inertia of motion of the passenger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This phenomenon is a direct application of **Newton’s First Law of Motion**, also known as the **Law of Inertia**. It states that an object will continue in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by an external **force** to change that state.
 
• **Inertia** is the inherent property of an object to resist any change in its state of motion. When the bus is moving, the passenger’s entire body is in a state of **motion** at the same **velocity** as the vehicle.
 
• When the bus suddenly stops, the lower part of the passenger’s body, which is in direct contact with the bus (through the feet or the seat), comes to **rest** along with the bus due to **friction**.
 
• However, the upper part of the passenger's body is not rigidly attached to the bus and, therefore, tends to maintain its state of **motion** due to **Inertia of Motion**.
 
• As a result, the upper body continues to move forward while the lower body stays still, causing the passenger to fall or lean forward. ***Hence, the correct answer is Inertia of motion of the passenger.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Inertia:**
 
 
• **Inertia of Rest:** The tendency of a body to remain in its state of rest. For example, when a bus suddenly starts, a passenger falls **backward** because the lower body moves with the bus while the upper body tries to remain at **rest**.
 
• **Inertia of Motion:** The tendency of a body to remain in its state of uniform motion. This is seen when a passenger falls **forward** when brakes are applied.
 
• **Inertia of Direction:** The tendency of a body to resist a change in its direction of motion. For example, when a car takes a sharp **right turn**, the passengers are thrown toward the **left**.
 
 
 
• **Mass as a Measure of Inertia:**
 
 
• The **inertia** of an object depends solely on its **mass**. The greater the **mass** of an object, the greater its **inertia**.
 
• For instance, it is harder to stop a moving **truck** than a moving **bicycle** at the same speed because the truck has more **mass** and thus more **inertia of motion**.
 
 
 
• **External Force:**
 
 
• In this scenario, the **brakes** provide the external **force** required to change the state of the bus, but that force is not directly applied to the upper body of the passenger, which is why **inertia** dominates the movement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Galileo Galilei** was the first to propose the concept of **Inertia**, which was later formalized by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687** in his famous work, **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**.
 
• **Newton's First Law** defines **Force** qualitatively, while the **Second Law** (F = ma) defines it quantitatively.
 
• In everyday life, **seatbelts** in cars are designed specifically to counteract the **inertia of motion** during sudden stops or accidents, preventing the passengers from hitting the **dashboard** or **windshield**.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**, which serves as the standard numerical measure of **inertia** in the **International System of Units**.

questions.question: A person ignores regular vehicle maintenance. Which of the following is most likely to happen?

options.text: Better tyre grip and less pollution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poor engine performance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vehicle maintenance** is the practice of inspecting or testing the condition of vehicle subsystems (e.g., **engine**, **brakes**, **tires**) and servicing or replacing parts and fluids to ensure safety and efficiency.
 
• When a person ignores regular maintenance, the **internal combustion engine** suffers the most. Over time, **engine oil** loses its **viscosity** and becomes contaminated with debris, turning into "sludge" which fails to lubricate moving parts, leading to **excessive friction** and **poor engine performance**. ***Hence, the statement regarding poor engine performance is correct.***
 
• Neglect often leads to clogged **air filters**. A dirty filter restricts the flow of air into the **combustion chamber**, causing the engine to struggle to "breathe," which results in a loss of **horsepower** and sluggish acceleration.
 
• Ignoring **spark plug** replacement can lead to **engine misfires** and difficulty in starting the vehicle, further degrading the overall mechanical output and reliability of the car.
 
• Failure to maintain the **cooling system** (antifreeze/coolant levels) can lead to **engine overheating**, which can cause permanent structural damage like a **blown head gasket** or a cracked **engine block**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fuel Efficiency**: Contrary to option 1, neglecting maintenance leads to **decreased fuel efficiency**. Worn-out components and dirty sensors (like the **Oxygen sensor** or **MAF sensor**) cause the engine to burn more fuel than necessary to maintain speed.
 
• **Tire Grip and Safety**: Option 2 suggests better grip, but the reality is that neglected tires lose **tread depth**, leading to **hydroplaning** and reduced traction on wet roads. Improper **wheel alignment** and **tire pressure** also increase the risk of **blowouts**.
 
• **Environmental Impact**: Option 4 is incorrect because a poorly maintained engine undergoes **incomplete combustion**. This significantly **increases pollution** as the vehicle emits higher levels of **carbon monoxide (CO)**, **nitrogen oxides (NOx)**, and unburnt **hydrocarbons** through the exhaust.
 
• **Economic Consequences**: Regular servicing might seem expensive in the **short term**, but ignoring it leads to massive **repair costs** later. Furthermore, a vehicle with a poor maintenance record has a significantly lower **resale value** in the **automobile market**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Preventive Maintenance Schedule**: Most manufacturers recommend a minor service every **5,000 to 10,000 kilometers** and a major service every **20,000 to 40,000 kilometers**.
 
• **Check Engine Light**: This is a critical **diagnostic tool**. Ignoring this warning light can lead to the failure of the **catalytic converter**, which is one of the most expensive parts of the **exhaust system** to replace.
 
• **Braking System**: Maintenance includes checking **brake pads** and **brake fluid**. Neglect can lead to "brake fade," where the vehicle takes a much longer **stopping distance**, posing a **safety hazard** to the driver and pedestrians.
 
• **Battery Health**: Regular checks of the **battery terminals** for **corrosion** and ensuring the **alternator** is charging correctly prevent unexpected **electrical failures**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following represents a straight chain hydrocarbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Butane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **straight chain hydrocarbon** is an **aliphatic** compound in which all the **carbon atoms** are linked in a continuous, unbranched sequence.
 
• **Butane** (specifically **n-butane**) has the molecular formula **C4H10**. Its structure consists of four carbon atoms bonded in a row: **CH3-CH2-CH2-CH3**. Since there are no side branches attached to the main chain, it is a **straight chain hydrocarbon**. ***Hence, Butane is the correct option.***
 
• **Isobutane**, also known as **2-methylpropane**, is an **isomer** of butane with the same formula **C4H10**. However, it features a **branched chain** where a **methyl group** is attached to the second carbon atom of a three-carbon chain. ***Hence, this represents a branched chain.***
 
• **Benzene** has the molecular formula **C6H6**. It is a **cyclic** hydrocarbon characterized by a **hexagonal ring** with alternating double bonds. It is classified as an **aromatic** hydrocarbon rather than an open straight chain. ***Hence, this represents a cyclic structure.***
 
• **Cyclopentane** is a **cycloalkane** with the molecular formula **C5H10**. It consists of five carbon atoms arranged in a **closed-ring** structure. ***Hence, this is a cyclic hydrocarbon.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrocarbons:** These are **organic compounds** composed entirely of **hydrogen** and **carbon** atoms. They are the primary constituents of **petroleum** and **natural gas**.
 
• **Classification of Aliphatic Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• **Saturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes):** These contain only **single bonds** between carbon atoms. Examples include **Methane**, **Ethane**, and **Propane**.
 
• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons:** These contain at least one **double bond** (**Alkenes** like **Ethene**) or **triple bond** (**Alkynes** like **Ethyne**).
 
 
 
• **Open Chain vs. Closed Chain:**
 
 
• **Acyclic (Open Chain):** Carbon atoms are joined in a linear or branched manner. **Straight chains** have no branches, while **branched chains** have at least one carbon atom bonded to more than two other carbons.
 
• **Cyclic (Closed Chain):** Carbon atoms form one or more **rings**. These are subdivided into **alicyclic** (like **cyclohexane**) and **aromatic** (like **naphthalene**).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Butane:** It is a highly **flammable**, colorless, and easily **liquefied gas** at room temperature. It is commonly used as a fuel in **LPG** (Liquefied Petroleum Gas), **cigarette lighters**, and as a **propellant** in aerosol sprays.
 
• **Isomerism:** This is a phenomenon where compounds have the **same molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**. **Butane** and **Isobutane** are classic examples of **structural isomers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature:** The prefix "**n-**" (normal) is often used to denote **straight chain** alkanes to distinguish them from their branched counterparts.
 
• **Bonding:** In straight chain alkanes like **Butane**, every carbon atom is **sp3 hybridized**, resulting in a **tetrahedral** geometry around each carbon.
 
• **Catenation:** The ability of **carbon** to form long **straight**, **branched**, or **cyclic** chains is due to its unique property of **catenation**, which allows it to form strong **covalent bonds** with other carbon atoms.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is true for mixtures but NOT for compounds?

options.text: Components are present in fixed ratio.
Components can be separated by physical methods.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Components can be separated by physical methods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Physical Separation**: The primary distinction between a mixture and a compound is the method of separation. Components of a **mixture** can be separated using **physical methods** such as **filtration**, **evaporation**, **distillation**, **crystallization**, or **magnetization** because the substances are only physically blended. ***Hence, the statement "Components can be separated by physical methods" is true for mixtures.***
 
• **Fixed Ratio**: In a **compound**, elements are always present in a **fixed ratio by mass** (according to the **Law of Definite Proportions**). In contrast, the components of a **mixture** can be combined in **any proportion**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect for mixtures.***
 
• **Formation of New Substances**: A **compound** is a new substance formed through a **chemical reaction** where the constituent elements lose their identity. In a **mixture**, no **chemical bond** is formed, and thus no new chemical substance is created. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect for mixtures.***
 
• **Retention of Properties**: In a **mixture**, each constituent substance **retains its individual chemical and physical properties** (e.g., sugar in water still tastes sweet). In a **compound**, the properties of the product are entirely **different** from its constituent elements (e.g., **Water (H2O)** is a liquid, while **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen** are gases). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect for mixtures.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mixtures**: 
 
 
• A **mixture** contains two or more substances that are not chemically combined. 
 
• They are classified into two types: **Homogeneous mixtures** (uniform composition, e.g., **air**, **alloys** like **brass**) and **Heterogeneous mixtures** (non-uniform composition, e.g., **sand and salt**, **oil and water**).
 
• There is **no energy change** (absorption or evolution of heat/light) typically associated with the formation of a mixture.
 
 
 
• **Compounds**:
 
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more chemical elements are **chemically bonded** together.
 
• The types of bonds can be **covalent** or **ionic**.
 
• Compounds have a **fixed melting point** and **boiling point**, whereas mixtures show a range of temperatures.
 
• Separation of compounds requires **chemical** or **electrochemical reactions** like **electrolysis**.
 
 
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• **Common Salt (NaCl)** is a **compound**; it cannot be separated into **Sodium** and **Chlorine** by simple filtration.
 
• **Gunpowder** is a **mixture** of **nitre (potassium nitrate)**, **sulphur**, and **charcoal**, which can be separated using solvents or physical means.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Changes**: The formation of a **compound** involves a significant **change in energy**, usually in the form of **heat**, **light**, or **sound**. Mixtures are formed with little to no detectable energy change.
 
• **Homogeneity**: While all **compounds** are **homogeneous** in nature, **mixtures** can be either **homogeneous** or **heterogeneous**.
 
• **Identity**: The constituents of a **compound** lose their **chemical identity**, whereas the constituents of a **mixture** do not. For example, **Iron (Fe)** and **Sulphur (S)** mixed together can be separated by a magnet, but when heated to form **Iron Sulphide (FeS)**, the magnet no longer attracts the iron.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes parenchyma, a simple permanent tissue?

options.text: Parenchyma consists of dead, thick-walled cells without intercellular spaces.
Parenchyma is made of living, loosely arranged cells with thin walls that store food.
Parenchyma is a complex tissue found only in vascular bundles.
Parenchyma cells are highly specialised and tightly packed with no space between them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parenchyma is made of living, loosely arranged cells with thin walls that store food**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parenchyma** is the most common and fundamental type of **simple permanent tissue** found in plants.
 
• It consists of **living cells** that possess **thin cell walls** usually made of **cellulose**. They are generally **isodiametric** in shape, meaning they have approximately equal diameters in all directions.
 
• The cells are typically **loosely arranged**, which results in significant **intercellular spaces** between them. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct and statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Unlike **sclerenchyma**, which consists of dead cells with thickened lignified walls, **parenchyma** cells remain **metabolically active** throughout their life. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Parenchyma** is a **simple tissue** because it is composed of only **one type of cell** that is similar in structure and function. It is not a **complex tissue** like **Xylem** or **Phloem**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The primary **functions** of parenchyma include **food storage**, providing **turgidity** for mechanical support, and **secretion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specialized Parenchyma:**
 
 
• **Chlorenchyma**: When **parenchyma** contains **chloroplasts** and performs **photosynthesis**, it is called **chlorenchyma**. This is primarily found in the **mesophyll** of leaves.
 
• **Aerenchyma**: In **aquatic plants** (hydrophytes), large **air cavities** are present in the **parenchyma** to provide **buoyancy**, allowing the plant to float. This variation is known as **aerenchyma**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other Simple Tissues:**
 
 
• **Collenchyma**: These cells are **living** and **elongated** with **unevenly thickened corners** due to the deposition of **cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin**. They provide **flexibility** and **mechanical strength** to young stems and **petioles**.
 
• **Sclerenchyma**: These are **dead cells** at maturity, characterized by **highly thickened walls** containing **lignin**. They provide **stiffness** and **rigidity** to plant parts, such as the **husk of a coconut**.
 
 
 
• **Location**: **Parenchyma** is distributed throughout the plant body, including the **pith**, **cortex** of roots and stems, **mesophyll** of leaves, and the **flesh of fruits**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Simple vs. Complex Tissues**: **Simple tissues** (Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma) consist of **homogeneous cells**. **Complex tissues** (Xylem and Phloem) consist of **heterogeneous cells** (different types of cells working together as a unit).
 
• **Cell Wall Composition**: The **thin walls** of **parenchyma** allow for the easy exchange of materials and **osmosis**. In **storage parenchyma**, the walls may store **hemicellulose** as a reserve food material.
 
• **Regeneration**: Because **parenchyma** cells are **living** and maintain the ability to **divide** (totipotency), they play a crucial role in **wound healing** and **regeneration** in plants.
 
• **Date of Discovery**: The term **Parenchyma** was coined by **Nehemiah Grew** in the **17th century**, who is often referred to as the **Father of Plant Anatomy**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct property of solids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solids have strong intermolecular forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Matter** is anything that occupies space and has mass. It exists primarily in three states: **Solid**, **Liquid**, and **Gas**. A **solid** is defined by its structural **rigidity** and resistance to changes in shape or volume.
 
• In the **solid state**, the constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) are packed very closely together. The **intermolecular distances** are extremely short, which leads to **strong intermolecular forces** of attraction that hold the particles in **fixed positions**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Compressibility** is the measure of the relative volume change of a fluid or solid as a response to a pressure change. Because there is negligible space between the particles of a **solid**, they cannot be forced significantly closer together. Therefore, solids are **highly incompressible** and **rigid**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Solids maintain a **definite shape**, **definite volume**, and **definite mass**. Unlike liquids, which take the shape of the container, or gases, which expand to fill the entire volume of a container, solids keep their form regardless of the vessel. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Diffusion** is the process of particles spreading out from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration. In solids, the particles can only **oscillate** about their mean positions and do not move from one place to another. Consequently, the rate of **diffusion** in solids is extremely low or negligible compared to liquids and gases. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Solids:**
 
 
• **Crystalline Solids:** These possess a **regular** and repeating three-dimensional arrangement of particles throughout the crystal. They have sharp **melting points** and are considered **true solids**. Examples include **Diamond**, **Graphite**, and **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**.
 
• **Amorphous Solids:** These consist of particles arranged in an **irregular** or short-range order. They do not have sharp melting points and soften over a range of **temperatures**. They are often called **pseudo-solids** or **super-cooled liquids**. Examples include **Glass**, **Rubber**, and **Plastic**.
 
 
 
• **Intermolecular Forces:** These include **London dispersion forces**, **dipole-dipole interactions**, and **hydrogen bonding**. In solids, these forces are strong enough to overcome the **thermal energy** that would otherwise cause particles to move apart.
 
• **Density:** Generally, solids have a higher **density** than liquids and gases because the particles are **tightly packed**. A notable exception is **ice**, which is less dense than liquid water due to its open-cage hexagonal structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This theory explains that the **kinetic energy** of particles in a **solid** is very low. Since the energy is insufficient to break the **intermolecular bonds**, the particles remain locked in a specific **lattice structure**.
 
• **Effect of Temperature:** When a solid is heated, its **thermal energy** increases, causing the particles to vibrate more violently. Eventually, at the **melting point**, the thermal energy overcomes the **strong intermolecular forces**, and the solid transitions into a **liquid** state (fusion).
 
• **Isotropy and Anisotropy:** **Crystalline solids** are **anisotropic**, meaning physical properties like electrical resistance or refractive index show different values when measured along different directions. In contrast, **amorphous solids** are **isotropic**, showing identical properties in all directions.
 
• **Volume and Pressure:** Unlike gases, where the **volume** is highly dependent on **pressure** (Boyle's Law), the **volume** of a solid remains virtually constant under ordinary changes in pressure.
</ul

questions.question: What is the benefit of seed dispersal in plants?

options.text: It promotes the availability of mineral nutrients to plants.
It enables plants to expand their distribution.
It makes more water available to plants.
It increases competition between plants for sunlight.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It enables plants to expand their distribution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Seed dispersal** is the biological process by which **seeds are carried away** from the parent plant to different locations for germination.
 
• The most significant benefit of this process is that it allows plant species to **colonize new areas** and **expand their distribution** across various geographical regions. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 2.***
 
• It plays a crucial role in **preventing overcrowding** in a single area, which ensures that young seedlings do not have to struggle for survival in the shadow of the parent plant.

questions.question: A woman using a copper-T complains of abdominal pain and discomfort. What is the likely reason?

options.text: Uterine irritation caused by the IUD

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterine irritation caused by the IUD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Copper-T** is a type of **Intrauterine Device (IUD)** that is inserted into the **uterus** to prevent pregnancy. Because it is a **foreign object**, the body may react to its presence, leading to **uterine irritation** and subsequent **abdominal discomfort**.
 
• When an **IUD** is inserted, it can cause the **uterine muscles** to contract or cramp as they adjust to the device. This physical **irritation** of the **endometrium** (uterine lining) is the most common cause of localized pain. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Infection in the stomach** is usually caused by **bacteria** or **viruses** ingested through food or water and is physiologically unrelated to the placement of a contraceptive device in the **reproductive tract**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Copper-T** is a **non-hormonal** contraceptive method. It works through the release of **copper ions** rather than chemicals like **estrogen** or **progesterone** found in **tablets**; therefore, it does not cause **hormonal imbalance** associated with oral pills. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While certain **infections** (like PID) can lead to complications, a **blockage in the fallopian tube** is generally a cause of **infertility** and does not typically manifest as immediate abdominal discomfort specifically triggered by the presence of a **Copper-T**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

questions.question: In a parallel combination of resistors, which of the following quantities remains the same across all the resistors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The potential difference (V)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **parallel combination** of resistors, the **potential difference (V)** remains the **same** across every individual resistor. This occurs because all resistors are connected directly across the same **two nodes** or points of the circuit. ***Hence, the statement regarding potential difference is correct.***
 
• The total **electric current (I)** in a parallel circuit is the **sum of the currents** flowing through each branch. If the resistances are different, the current through each resistor will also be different. ***Hence, the statement regarding electric current is incorrect.***
 
• The **equivalent resistance (Req)** of the combination is calculated using the reciprocal formula: **1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn**. The **Req** is always **smaller** than the smallest individual resistance in the group. ***Hence, the statement regarding equivalent resistance is incorrect.***
 
• The **power consumed (P)** by each resistor depends on its resistance value. Since **P = V²/R** and **V** is constant, the resistor with the **least resistance** will consume the **most power**. ***Hence, the statement regarding power consumed is incorrect.***
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, which is **V = IR**, the current through each branch in a parallel circuit is **inversely proportional** to its **resistance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Combination**: Unlike parallel circuits, in a **series combination**, the **electric current (I)** remains the same through all resistors, while the **potential difference (V)** is distributed across them based on their resistance values.
 
• **Household Wiring**: Most **domestic electrical circuits** are connected in **parallel**. This ensures that every appliance receives the **standard voltage** (e.g., **220V in India**) and can be turned on or off independently without affecting other devices.
 
• **Circuit Reliability**: In a **parallel circuit**, if one resistor or appliance **fails** or the path is broken, the **current** can still flow through the other parallel branches, allowing the rest of the system to function.
 
• **Total Current Calculation**: The total current **I** leaving the **voltage source** is equal to **V / Req**. This total current splits into different paths (**I1, I2, etc.**) and recombines before returning to the source.
 
• **Applications**: Parallel combinations are used in **power grids**, **car headlights**, and **computer hardware** to maintain constant operating **voltages** across multiple components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Potential Difference (V)**: Measured in **Volts (V)** using a **voltmeter**, which is always connected in **parallel** to the component.
 
• **Electric Current (I)**: Measured in **Amperes (A)** using an **ammeter**, which is always connected in **series** within a branch.
 
• **Resistance (R)**: Measured in **Ohms (Ω)**. In parallel, adding more resistors **decreases** the total **equivalent resistance** of the circuit.
 
• **Short Circuit**: If a branch with **zero resistance** is connected in parallel with other resistors, all the current will flow through that branch, effectively **bypassing** the others.
